properties.description: The Flaten Art Barn, which opened fall 2013 in its new location adjacent to the wind turbine, is a reconstruction of a 1932 building that served as the first home of the college's Art Department. It is named after its designer/builder and the founder of what is now the Department of Art and Art History, Arnold Flaten.
properties.name: Flaten Art Barn

properties.description: The Ade Christenson Complex on the east side of campus is home to Klein Field at Manitou, the Manitou Track, and Tom Porter Hall. The playing and running surfaces are first-class competition sites for the football and men's and women's track and field teams. Two classrooms, locker rooms, an athletic training room, offices for coaches and staff, and a weight room make Tom Porter Hall a convenient home to the football, track and field, and men's and women's hockey teams. The lobby overlooks the west end zone and track, and it has a clear view of the bleachers and press box. The venue is also the home of the college's commencement ceremonies.
properties.name: Ade Christenson Complex

properties.description: Holland Hall was dedicated in 1925 as part of the celebrations for the college's 50th anniversary. Architects for the building drew inspiration for the building's design from Mon-Saint-Michel, the fortress monastery on the coast of Normandy, France. In particular, they designed it to resemble the Merville - the monastery's assembly hall and dining area. Although the power plant built in 1935 was the first building on campus to display the limestone-studded Norma Gothic style that has become the hallmark of the Hill, it wasn't until Holland Hall was built that the architectural style made its full impact. Longtime faculty member Peter Olai Holland, who also served as the college's treasurer and director of finance, was St. Olaf President Lars W. Boe's "right-hand man". Related Links St. Olaf College News - November 1, 2017: The new Holland Hall

properties.description: The Hall of Music, which opened in February 2012, provides extended space for the Music Department. Complementing Christiansen Hall of Music, the new Hall of Music (more commonly known as the "Music Box") hosts 36 practice rooms, including two concerto rooms with two grand pianos; four chamber music rehearsal spaces; a reed room for double reeds; a percussion suite; 12 faculty studios; and the Music Department office. The Hall of Music connects with Alumni Hall to the west and the Center for Art and Dance (home to the Art/Art History and Dance departments) to the east. Related Links Music Department

properties.description: Built by members of the St. Olaf community over the summer of 2003, this Scandinavian-style wooden tower commemorates the lives of students who have died while enrolled at St. Olaf. The chimes, tuned to the key of F. Melius Christiansen’s iconic hymn “Beautiful Savior,” are engraved with the names of those students. On windy days, the sound of the chimes can be heard almost everywhere on campus. It serves as a precious and beautiful reminder of those we have lost both past and present here on the Hill.
properties.name: Memorial Chime Tower

Through the years, Old Main has housed various departments in the humanities and now is home to the Religion Department. The hill to the east of the building is a popular sledding venue for students and local neighbors.

properties.description: Rand Hall, nestled into the north face of Manitou Heights, houses 243 upper-class men and women. A variety of living options are available in Rand including single, double, and quad occupancy rooms. Suites share their own bathrooms. The hillside location offers a beautiful view of the woods and fields surrounding the college.
properties.name: Rand Hall

properties.description: Completed in 1942 and named in honor of 1905 alumnus Ole Rolvaag, former St. Olaf professor of Norwegian and author of Giants in the Earth, Rolvaag Library is the largest of three libraries on the St. Olaf campus (the others are the Hustad Science Library in Regents Hall and then Halvorson Music Library in Christiansen Hall of Music). Special Collections and College Archives are located on the second floor of Rolvaag Memorial Library. The Halvorson Music Library is located in the Christiansen Hall of Music. The fourth floor of Rolvaag is home to the Information Technology (IT) Department and the Digital Scholarship Center (DiSCO), which provides the campus community assistance with technology and digital scholarship. The English Department and classrooms are located on the fifth floor of the library in the original section of the building. Related Links College Archives Digital Scholarship Center (DiSCO) English Department Information Technology (IT) Hong Kierkegaard Library - The Hong Kierkegaard Library is now located in Steensland Hall Information Technology (IT) Helpdesk Norwegian American Historical Association (NAHA) Special Collections
properties.name: Rolvaag Memorial Library

The building - along with the adjacent Regents Hall of Natural Sciences - has become an invaluable teaching tool for the nearly 40 percent of St. Olaf students who pursue a major or concentration in the natural sciences or mathematics. Related Links Computer Science Mathematical Biology Mathematics Statistics
properties.name: Regents Hall of Mathematical Sciences

properties.description: With such features as a green roof, aggressive daylighting, and the minimization of chemical and biological waste, LEED Platinum-certified Regents Hall is not simply a model for responsible environmental stewardship, but a daily working example of sustainability in practice. Since opening in fall 2008, the building - along with the adjacent Regents Hall of Mathematical Sciences - has become an invaluable teaching tool for nearly 40 percent of St. Olaf students who pursue a major or concentration in the natural sciences or mathematics. Related Links Biology Biomolecular Science Chemistry Environmental Studies Mathematical Biology Natural Lands Neuroscience Nursing Physics Psychology
properties.name: Regents Hall of Natural Sciences

properties.description: Skoglund Center hosts varsity basketball and volleyball games in its 2008-seat arena, and its natatorium is home to the swimming and diving teams. Men's Basketball Women's Basketball Volleyball Skoglund also has a field house, racquetball courts, wrestling room, locker rooms, an athletic training room, and is home to the Kinesiology Department. Outdoor tennis courts are located behind the building, near the softball, baseball and soccer fields. In addition to housing athletics, Skoglund Center is used for large ensemble performances - including the annual St. Olaf Christmas Festival.
properties.name: Skoglund Athletic Center and Auditorium

properties.description: Hector Skifter Hall houses the administrative offices for Broadcast Media and extended practice/studio space for the Music Department. Home to the college's organ studies, Skifter Hall has been specifically redesigned and renovated to house several practice organs and rehearsal spaces acoustically engineered for the instrument. The Tormodsgaard-Bakken Recital Hall (Studio A) contains a Dobson three-manual tracker organ and is used for studio sessions, musical instruction, and rehearsals.
properties.name: Skifter Hall

properties.description: Located on the second floor of Buntrock Commons, Stav Hall is the central dining room on campus. It offers students and guests all-you-can-eat dining for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Stations throughout the cafeteria offer a wide variety of food, from chef-carved meats with home-style casseroles to creative vegan entrees to pan-Asian cuisine. Stav Hall also features two soups made in house daily, an extensive fruit and salad bar, and a selection of outstanding desserts.
properties.name: Stav Hall

properties.description: STOGROW, the on-campus farm of approximately 1.5 acres, is an entirely student-run community initiative. Each winter, a number of students are hired to work on the farm during the following summer and throughout the growing season, in addition to taking a course in the spring centered around sustainable farming practices. Students are able to directly apply lessons about agriculture that they have learned during their course, while also making decisions about what works best for them as they progress. STOGROW provides a place for students to practice and troubleshoot farming, learn from mistakes, and focus on improvement without worrying too much about the bottom line. Related Links Natural Lands Natural Lands Maps
properties.name: STOGROW Farm
